extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, researchers, librarians, and users of MathSciNet/Mathematical Reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the editorial practices, reviewer expectations, and bibliometric metric (MCQ) used by the American Mathematical Society's Mathematical Reviews / MathSciNet service. Covers coverage goals, reviewer selection, allowed review content, language policy, and how the Mathematical Citation Quotient is computed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal: comprehensive coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal of the new journal was to give reviews of every mathematical research publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mathematical Reviews aims for comprehensive coverage of mathematical research publications; the database has been built to index a very large number of articles (over 2.2 million as of 2007).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection: expertise-based volunteer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors of reviews are volunteers, usually chosen by the editors because of some expertise in the area of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are selected by editors for topical expertise; reviews are produced by volunteer mathematicians rather than by paid staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of reviews: detailed summaries and references
rubrics_metrics.description: Often reviews give detailed summaries of the contents of the paper, sometimes with critical comments by the reviewer and references to related work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred review content includes a clear summary of the paper's contents and references to related literature; critical comments may appear but are not the primary focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constraint on criticism: reviewers not encouraged to criticize
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are not encouraged to criticize the paper, because the author does not have an opportunity to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical or harsh evaluative language is discouraged in reviews since the reviewed author cannot reply; emphasis is on exposition rather than polemics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of author's summary when independent review impossible
rubrics_metrics.description: The author's summary may be quoted when it is not possible to give an independent review, or when the summary is deemed adequate by the reviewer or the editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reviewer cannot produce an independent assessment (for example, due to language barriers or other limitations), quoting the author's own summary is acceptable when judged adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal entry (bibliographic-only) in special cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Only bibliographic information may be given when a work is in an unusual language, when it is a brief paper in a conference volume, or when it is outside the primary scope of the Reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In cases of language difficulty, very short/insubstantial items, or material outside MR's scope, the appropriate response is a bibliographic citation without a substantive review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language policy: English-only reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Originally the reviews were written in several languages, but later an "English only" policy was introduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews are expected to be in English under the current policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical Citation Quotient (MCQ) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The MCQ is calculated by counting the total number of citations into the journal that have been indexed by Mathematical Reviews over a five-year period, and dividing this total by the total number of papers published by the journal during that five-year period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MCQ is an MR-specific bibliometric analogous to an impact factor; it uses a five-year citation window and MR-indexed citations only.

rubrics_metrics.name: All Journal MCQ (comparison baseline)
rubrics_metrics.description: The "All Journal MCQ" is computed by considering all the journals indexed by Mathematical Reviews as a single meta-journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All Journal MCQ provides a baseline to determine if a particular journal's MCQ is higher or lower than the MR-indexed average (example: 2018 All Journal MCQ = 0.41).
